Header: Acrosporium mangiferae ( syn. Odium erysiphoides f. mangiferae )

Prevention: Plantations must be established far away from unattended mango trees.
Clear weeds and prune trees to improve aeration to reduce the disease spread.
Intercrop with onion or forestry trees to reduces the ease with which the disease affect the mango.
Monitoring: Monitor field weekly from start of flowering period until fruit formation.
Look for small patches of white powdery substance (mycelium), which may later add together to cover large areas on leaves.
Do not mistake with the waxy light- green whitish patches along inner veins of mango leaves that are natural.
On older leaves and fruit, look for purplish-brown cast as the white growth weathers away.
Scout for abortive inflorescence or flowers that fail to open and drop from the panicles.
If 2 to 3 trees are infested (5 to 10% of leaves or flower bunches) out of 10 trees, then consider action.
Direct Control: Apply potassium dihydrogen phosphate at the rate of 25g/100mls of water to prevent the spread of powdery mildew.
It can be combined with fungicides effectively.
Remove severely infected panicles and destroy by burying or burning.
Use mancozeb based products (Agarithan 80WP, Contizeb 80WP etc) as foliar spray at early sign of infection at the rate of 30-50mls/15l of water.
It acts as broad spectrum preventive fungicide.
